races.name: Power Utilities Group Conditional Jockeys' Selling Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Pigeon House
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here with winning form at 16f on good ground and a yard T14 record of 0/0, suggesting stable is quiet; 49 days off and a pull to OR 118 make this interesting as a pace-controlling lead horse, and the p headgear flag suggests it has form in a hood.|

runners_data.name: At The Oche
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse with four consecutive second places before a recent win (1B form), trained by in-form Dan Skelton (T14: 7/17) and ridden by a 3lb claimer reducing the weight; 13 days since last run, good-ground record of 9/11, and a natural prominent style well-suited to tracking a single front-runner at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Mountain Port
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator over 16-20f with a laboured recent record (770-0) and a specific finish-fade warning flag; 64 days off for Daisy Hitchins (T14: 0/6) on a trip and going where historical figures read 7-7-7-12-14 — hard to make a case at any price without improvement.|

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Repeated placer at 16f on good ground (4-4-3 in last three starts) who races from off the pace; James Owen's yard has been busy (T14: 2/36) and 9 days between runs is a short turnaround, but this horse's consistent placed form suggests it stays competitive without necessarily winning.|

runners_data.name: Mojo Ego
runners_data.note: Won at 16f on good ground last time and has Fergal O'Brien in decent 14-day form (1/7); a natural deep-closer whose actual racing position will likely be further back than the midfield slot shown on the map, meaning it needs things to fall its way tactically in a race where the pace is controlled rather than truly strong.|

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with six recent runs all producing placed finishes (421353), a good-ground record of 9/15, and course/trip experience over 17-18f; Nick Scholfield's yard is ticking over (T14: 2/15) and the tb headgear has been a stable feature — races close enough to matter if the leader tires.|

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's runner (T14: 0/7) has been off 48 days and arrives with form figures of 039PP, the double P particularly concerning; a true hold-up horse in natural style who is placed into a midfield slot only because the rear is crowded, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects real doubt about whether it can reproduce its best from a compromised tactical position.|

races.paceDynamic: Pigeon House is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset — this is not a race where the pace is forced or injected artificially. At The Oche and Raffles Nobu will track prominently just off the leader, creating a compact front group through the early and middle stages. The hold-up contingent — Versatile, Mountain Port, Chillhi, and Mojo Ego — will be settled in behind, though Chillhi and Mojo Ego are genuine deep closers redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate all of them at the rear simultaneously. The race shape heavily favours a prominent racer who can travel smoothly just off the steady pace Pigeon House sets and pounce from a close enough position, as the lack of real pressure through the race makes it extremely difficult for true hold-up horses to find the winning gap late on good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Pigeon House sets a fair but unforced gallop and At The Oche or Raffles Nobu track the leader before striking two out.
scenarios.body: The controlled pace means a horse travelling prominently conserves energy and arrives at the final obstacles with a decisive advantage over anything coming from off the pace; good ground at Stratford over this trip rewards those who travel in a rhythm close to the leader rather than making up ground. At The Oche's recent form (four consecutive placings on similar going), trainer Skelton's sharp 14-day record, and Raffles Nobu's consistent proximity running make this profile the overwhelmingly dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Pigeon House's conditional jockey Beau Morgan dictates a truly modest pace and the field is slow to react coming off the final bend.
scenarios.body: Pigeon House has winning form at 16f on good ground with a pull in the weights here, and a solo leader who is never pressured can coast to the line if the chasing pack leaves the challenge too late; the longer trip of 2m2½f at Stratford gives a fresh leader time to regulate reserves. OR 118 means this horse has class to exploit an uncontested lead even at this level of conditional jockeys' selling company.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to burn off the prominent horses and leave a late gap for a closer — unlikely given the single front-runner setup.
scenarios.body: Versatile has shown repeated placed efforts on good ground at this sort of trip and Mojo Ego has a course-valid win, but both rely on the pace collapsing rather than being manufactured, making this scenario dependent on an unlikely pace meltdown. The redistribution of Mojo Ego and Chillhi means neither is operating in their truest role, and STYLE_FIT scores of 0.93 and 0.91 respectively temper confidence that either can replicate deep-closing form from a more forward position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a chaotic landing off the final flight cause the race to break up and produce an unpredictable result.
scenarios.body: Mountain Port's warning flag for fading finishes and form figures of 770-0 suggest a tail-ender rather than a scrambled winner, while Chillhi's PP form over fences and hurdles flags unreliability; neither inspires confidence even in a chaotic shape. This scenario is a catch-all for unseats, falls or errors that reshuffle the order at the last, not a realistic profiling edge.

watchPoints.text: Watch Pigeon House's early jumping — if Beau Morgan (conditional) gets the lead cleanly and settles, the entire race dynamic revolves around whether anything can close on a horse dictating its own fractions.
At The Oche's jockey Harry Atkins holds a 3lb claim, but the Dan Skelton yard's 7/17 T14 strike rate makes this combination significant — watch for a prominent move on the home turn.

Mojo Ego and Chillhi are both natural hold-up horses mapped forward of their true position; if the pace is genuinely slow, neither may get the run of things they need, and backers should note both STYLE_FIT flags before concluding they can dominate from mid-division.

Mountain Port's finish-fade tag over 12-20f on good ground and T14 of 0/6 for the Hitchins yard suggests connections are not going into this in particularly strong form — monitor in-running for early signs of the horse travelling poorly.

races.name: What The Frunk: The Geely Ex2 Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Gambino
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (two wins on Good ground at 17f) and handled by the powerful Skelton operation, but with Pioneer Pete and Tazman Dan dominating the early positions, this horse is unlikely to get its natural place near the front and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: King's Scholar
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good ground and consistent prominent racing make this a natural fit for the pace shape; Tom Hutsby claims 10lb and the 100-day absence is the key question, but Olly Murphy's 2/8 in the past fortnight suggests the yard is in form.

runners_data.name: Pioneer Pete
runners_data.note: The dominant force in this race shape — eight runs on similar going, two wins, and a front-running style that sets the agenda; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. gives him a high-class pilot and his last win came over the same course and distance trip.

runners_data.name: Tazman Dan
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner returning after 153 days off for Stuart Edmunds, whose 0/0 recent strike rate offers no confidence; sim-going record is a bare 1/3 with no wins, and a fitness question mark makes it likely Pioneer Pete will assert dominance in the duel.

runners_data.name: Bailey's Luck
runners_data.note: Has a hold-up profile but the fade warning is alarming alongside a form string of P0 and a poor sim-going record of 2/3 with no wins; Ben Poste takes over and age (4) means scope for improvement, but this is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Don't Rein Me In
runners_data.note: Returns from 167 days off with a mixed record on Good ground (one second from four runs) and Bryan Carver partnering for Chris Honour, who has no recent runners; the moderate form string 2047 does not inspire confidence at this level despite prominent racing tendencies.

runners_data.name: Northwest Passage
runners_data.note: Apprentice William Shanahan (5lb claim) rides for Ivan Furtado, whose 0/17 recent record is a significant red flag; sim-going figures (0W2P from 7 runs) suggest the horse rarely threatens on Good ground, and stepping up from 10-12f trips to 2m½f is a substantial jump.

races.paceDynamic: Pioneer Pete and Tazman Dan are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 2m½f trip on Good ground at Stratford, creating an honest, competitive gallop from flagfall rather than any dawdling tactical affair. Pioneer Pete holds the stronger profile in similar going (8/9 sim-going record, two wins) and is likely to assert supremacy up front under Jonjo O'Neill Jr., with Tazman Dan pushing him throughout before the race tests stamina entering the final circuit. Gambino is a natural prominent racer but, with two genuine lead-seekers dominating that space, is unlikely to secure its preferred position and has been mapped to midfield accordingly — the field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, and King's Scholar and Don't Rein Me In are the prominent runners most likely to actually land close to the pace given their profiles and jockeys. This contested pace suits a horse able to travel smoothly in mid-division and sustain a run from two out — the profile that benefits most is a well-settled prominent-to-midfield type with proven form on Good ground who can pick off a tiring leader at the business end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pioneer Pete Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Pioneer Pete asserts from the break and Tazman Dan cannot sustain the duel, leaving a clear lead by halfway.
scenarios.body: Pioneer Pete's dominant sim-going record (8/9, 2W) and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. in the saddle give him the tools to dictate a strong but controlled gallop that grinds rivals into submission; with Tazman Dan potentially fading after a prolonged duel, the leader simply needs to jump cleanly and keep tabs on the next hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Fatigues Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the Pioneer Pete–Tazman Dan duel burns both leaders out, leaving a prominent racer to coast through on the bridle late.
scenarios.body: King's Scholar, who has winning form on Good ground at this trip and can race handily without over-committing, would be ideally placed to pick up the pieces; Don't Rein Me In, fresh off 167 days and racing at a shorter price in a novice context, could also close strongly if the pace collapse is severe.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly brutal from flag to finish and the field strings out, creating an opportunity for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Bailey's Luck is the only genuine hold-up runner in the field but carries a stamina-fade warning and poor recent form (P0), making this scenario structurally weak; Don't Rein Me In has some hold-up capacity and is the more credible closer if ground gives enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Tazman Dan underperforms after 153 days off and Pioneer Pete is left to coast in front unchallenged at a crawl, inviting a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A sprint finish would favour horses with sharp acceleration rather than pure stamina, and the redistribution of Gambino into midfield means it is racing out of role, diluting its chance even in this shape; Northwest Passage and King's Scholar, with modest flat-speed profiles, would be the marginal beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Pioneer Pete and Tazman Dan will fight for the lead from the first hurdle — watch whether Tazman Dan can sustain the duel past halfway, because a dominant escape by Pioneer Pete transforms this from a contested shape into a procession.

Gambino is racing out of its natural prominent role and mapped to midfield by force rather than preference; if the pace dissolves early and positions open up, it may push forward, creating a traffic bunching risk between hurdles three and five.

Tazman Dan is returning after 153 days off with no recent trainer runners and a trainer in Stuart Edmunds who has a blank 14-day record — monitor at the start for any fitness-related sluggishness that could alter the entire pace map.

King's Scholar is the 100-day returner most likely to benefit from an honest gallop — watch for Tom Hutsby positioning him just off the lead pair from the outset, as any traffic trouble in midfield would compromise his challenge significantly.

Bailey's Luck's fade-in-finish tag makes it a horse to watch early for signs of being pulled up or hampered; if it causes interference in the rear of the field off a contested early pace, runners held up behind could lose significant ground.

races.name: Allan Atkinson Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Jet Patrol
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with strong Good-ground profile (11 runs, 2 wins, 4 places in similar conditions) and Sean Bowen in the saddle is a significant positive; five recent runs all over 16f on Good gives him the ideal course-shape profile, though his OR of 97 means he carries the most weight in the field.

runners_data.name: Langton Wold
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose last five runs include a mix of shorter trips and flat-style tracks, making the jumping and stamina demands here a genuine question; Nathan Moscrop takes over, and while the Going suits, his recent form (64322/) tailed off after a promising second over 16f on Good, and a return to hurdling could see him find less than hoped.

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has won over this exact trip and going combination (1/16f/GOO) and has a live chance if he can control the pace rather than fight for it; the presence of Genbu and Saucats makes that scenario harder than usual, and Brendan Powell will need to decide early whether to contest or concede, with the F in recent form a minor flag for jumping reliability.

runners_data.name: Lord Of The Glance
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up/prominent type with an outstanding recent record for consistency on Good ground (1W3P in last five similar-going runs), and Toby McCain-Mitchell (3) takes the ride off a quick seven-day turnaround; the 2m½f trip looks ideal and he has repeatedly shown a strong finishing effort when given a clear run.

runners_data.name: Western Soldier
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up handler who is 67 days off a run, which is a fitness concern, and Benjamin Macey (5) is a claim jockey on a horse who hasn't hit the track since spring; Good ground suits and he has placed at 16f and 18f in this going, but the layoff and apprentice booking both need to be discounted appropriately.

runners_data.name: Connemara Joe
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose natural tendency is to race from the rear, but in this pace-heavy field he is likely to be pushed further forward than ideal — his entire four-run sample on Good shows 0 wins, 0 places, which is a flat statistical read, and the tp headgear hasn't unlocked a win yet; Stan Sheppard rides for the small Sheppard yard.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Front-runner piloted by amateur Mr Sam Burton (7) who carries the most significant jockey allowance weight discount in the field; the U in recent form is an obvious jumping concern, and while he has placed on Good ground earlier in his career, his form has deteriorated markedly through the current campaign.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: The most consistent of the three pace-setters with 13 runs in similar going and a 1W5P record, plus a recent win at 18f and two places over 18f on Good ground; Callum Pritchard continues the partnership and the tp headgear suggests he needs caution to settle, which is tested severely by Mayday Games and Genbu pushing from the front.

runners_data.name: Battle Stride
runners_data.note: Four-year-old carrying a clear flag for fading in the finish — a concern in a stamina race like this — and after 52 days off the course he comes here fresh but potentially needing the run; his natural inclination is to race from the rear but the pace of this field is likely to find him closer than comfortable, and the 0W0P record in similar going on Good is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Raincloud
runners_data.note: Significantly the lowest-rated runner (OR 68) and 105 days off the track — the longest layoff in the field — making fitness the primary question; his recent form string (99P8-8) includes a pulled-up and two ninth-place finishes, and while Good ground is familiar, his history is over longer trips of 20-23f, making this 2m½f trip potentially too sharp for his style.

races.paceDynamic: Mayday Games, Genbu, and Saucats are all confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off at Stratford over 2m½f on Good ground, making a strong, sustained gallop virtually certain. This three-way battle for early supremacy will stretch the field out from the first hurdle, burning through stamina reserves and setting up a searching test that will expose any weakness in the closing stages. Jet Patrol, as the highest-rated prominent runner, is ideally placed to track the pace without getting embroiled in the early scrap, while the genuine hold-up horses — Connemara Joe, Battle Stride, and Raincloud — are unlikely to secure their natural rear positions given the volume of pace ahead of them; Lord Of The Glance and Western Soldier are better placed to access the race from a patient position. The race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile: horses who can sit just off the hot pace, conserve energy through the middle stages, and produce a sustained gallop from the second-last when the pace-setters begin to tie up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between Mayday Games, Genbu, and Saucats burns them all out before the final flight, setting up a clean run for the prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: Jet Patrol, tracking from a prominent position under Sean Bowen, is perfectly placed to capitalise as the leaders empty, with his consistent Good-ground form over 16f giving him the class edge in the finish. Lord Of The Glance's record of placing consistently on Good ground (1W3P in similar conditions) also makes him a threat as he picks off the fading leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pace-Setter Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the trio — most likely Saucats, who has the most consistent recent form and best Going record (13/15) — gets a soft lead after the others fade or make errors.
scenarios.body: Saucats has shown the ability to front-run and sustain an effort over 18f on Good ground, and a clean race from the front with the pace reduced could see him last home better than rivals expect. Mayday Games, who has won over this exact trip and going combination, must also be considered if he manages to wrestle control and dictate his own terms.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that it creates a truly fast-run race where even the stalkers are pulled into early trouble, leaving a genuine late run viable from the back.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally weaker because Connemara Joe, Battle Stride, and Raincloud are all redistributed runners who are unlikely to achieve their natural hold-up berths in a field this front-heavy, diminishing the chance they produce a true closing run. Western Soldier, who has placed over similar distances on Good ground, is the most realistic beneficiary among those with any hold-up tendency if the fractions are extreme.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Outbattle All
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a moderate pace in the middle of the race causes the field to compress, turning the race into a battle of attrition from three out where raw stamina and consistency count most.
scenarios.body: Lord Of The Glance, with four consecutive top-three finishes over Good ground at this sort of trip, thrives in a grinding contest, and Langton Wold — despite his flat-race pedigree and shorter recent history — showed ability to stay over 16f on Good.

watchPoints.text: Mayday Games, Genbu, and Saucats will all break forward immediately — watch the first two hurdles to see which, if any, gains a clean break; if all three are locked together by the third hurdle, a messy, over-pressured gallop is confirmed and stamina tests for the field become severe.

Genbu has an Unseated in his last six runs — watch his jumping at the early obstacles, as a riderless horse from a front-runner in a tightly-contested pace group could interfere with Jet Patrol and Lord Of The Glance who will be tracking close.

Western Soldier is 67 days absent and ridden by an apprentice — watch how quickly he settles and whether Macey can position him patiently; a too-keen early run off a layoff would compromise his stamina badly in this type of race.

Battle Stride carries a known tendency to fade in the finish and is 52 days off the track — watch for him dropping away sharply from the second-last if the race has been run at the expected strong tempo, as he could cause interference to the genuine closers behind him.

Lord Of The Glance runs on a quick seven-day turnaround — watch whether McCain-Mitchell settles him comfortably off the pace in the first mile, as his best form has come when able to produce a sustained run from the third-last rather than being asked to quicken sharply.

races.name: Wynchwood Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Breaking Cover
runners_data.note: Arrives on a 9-day turnaround after winning over 16f on Good ground, with a solid 4W7P similar-going record and Chad Bament's 5lb claim reducing the 168lb burden; held-up style suits this pace scenario perfectly, though the 2m1f trip is shorter than recent winning distances.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's yard is in form (T14: 1/9), Sean Quinlan takes the ride, and a remarkable 5W13P similar-going strike-rate underlines genuine class; prominent style is ideal for sitting just off a contested pace battle and pouncing late, with the 2m1f trip well within range.

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Harry Kimber takes over on a confirmed front-runner who is 41 days off the track and whose recent form reads 5-433P — a concern over this shorter trip against two rivals who will challenge for the same early lead; 0W3P on similar going adds to reservations.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: The 12-year-old has strong course experience and a 2W7P similar-going record, but at OR=124 and with a recent P in his last start, he will need to avoid a draining early battle with Sony Bill and Gower Prince; Sean D Bowen's tactical awareness could help him settle slightly off the pace if the other two front-runners press harder.

runners_data.name: In This World
runners_data.note: B R Summers has had 0 winners from 2 runners in the last 14 days, and In This World's form (P5-5F2) includes a fall and multiple out-of-the-frame finishes; the 2nd last time out at 17f on Good is the primary positive, but the hold-up style leaves him dependent on a truly strung-out field to find a clear run.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill's yard is cold (T14: 0/12), but Gower Prince himself has won and placed in two of his last three starts at 16-17f on Good — exactly this type of conditions; Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim helps carry 142lbs, and his front-running style means he may be the freshest and most economical of the three pace-setters if the other two fight harder than he does.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill, Sir Tivo, and Gower Prince are all confirmed front-runners in a field of just six, guaranteeing an honest, pressured gallop from the outset over 2m1f at Stratford. All three will be fighting for position early, meaning none can dictate entirely on their own terms — the pace will be genuine rather than manufactured, and the fractions are unlikely to ease at any point across the chase course. The two hold-up horses, Breaking Cover and In This World, will be afforded a rhythm and a target throughout, while Captain Cool's prominent style means he can sit just off the pace battle and pounce without expending energy in the early scramble. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent runners who can conserve energy behind a contested lead and finish powerfully — true front-runners are likely to face a war of attrition against each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill, Sir Tivo, and Gower Prince push each other through a contested gallop and burn out before the final obstacles.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners exhaust each other setting a hot pace, leaving the race wide open for those held up or tracking prominently into the straight; the 2m1f trip on Good ground at Stratford will expose any horse that has done too much work early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Captain Cool Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool slots in just behind the lead battle and produces a smooth, well-timed challenge from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: With a T14 strike-rate of 1/9 and the best recent course form profile of any non-frontrunner (5W13P on similar going), Captain Cool is ideally equipped to stalk the pace duel and assert; Sean Quinlan's experience on hold-up and prominent types gives him the tactical nous to time the move perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters — most likely Gower Prince or Sir Tivo — establishes a slight lead and repels the hold-up horses with enough left in reserve.
scenarios.body: Gower Prince's recent winning form (1st and 2nd in last two starts) and 13/15 similar-going record suggest he has the class to handle pressure, while Sir Tivo's course-and-distance experience at age 12 means he knows how to ration his effort; a strong-galloping survivor scenario would reward the front-runner who jumps cleanest and wastes least energy in the early exchanges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly scorching and In This World or Breaking Cover deliver a powerful late flourish over the final two fences.
scenarios.body: Breaking Cover arrives only 9 days fresh off a win at 16f on Good and has a 4W7P similar-going record to underpin a late run, while In This World's 2nd last time out shows residual ability if the gaps appear; the risk is that a six-runner field with three front-runners may cluster rather than string out, leaving hold-up horses with less room to weave through.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Sony Bill, Sir Tivo, and Gower Prince to clash for the lead at the first fence — if all three compete aggressively early, the race could be over for them by the fourth-last, dramatically boosting Breaking Cover and Captain Cool.

Gower Prince (T14: 0/12 for Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill) carries a cold-yard flag despite good personal form — if the training prep is not spot-on, his front-running role becomes a liability rather than an asset.

In This World's record includes a fall (F in recent form) and multiple mid-race exits — in a race where jumping fluency under pressure is critical, a jumping error at pace could affect the runners around him as well.

Captain Cool's similar-going record (5W13P from 13 qualifiers) stands out as the deepest, most reliable evidence base in the field — if he travels smoothly in third or fourth early, he is the horse to track visually through the race.

Breaking Cover's 9-day turnaround is tight but not unusual for Anthony Honeyball, and his last-run win means fitness is assured — watch whether Chad Bament settles him off the pace cleanly or if a crowded early field forces him wider than ideal.

races.name: Rich Ellis's 60th Vinyl Countdown Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Roaring Home
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with strong Good-ground form (10/15 sim-going, 3 wins) and solid recent record over 20-24f trips; Sam Twiston-Davies is an experienced pilot at this level and 49 days since last run is not a concern given the trainer's low recent strike rate suggesting patient placement.

runners_data.name: Porter In The Park
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with excellent course/distance credentials (13/15 sim-going) returning after 94 days off for Emma Lavelle's string, which has sent out 7 runners in 14 days; the amateur claimer (7lb) is a factor to weigh but the strong distance record at 26f makes her a live each-way type if fit.

runners_data.name: Jackstell
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent sort whose tongue-tie addition and Good-ground form (8/11, 4 wins) are positives; the recent trainer form (1/9 in 14 days) is modest but Jamie Snowden has placed this horse well before, and 67 days fresh is fine — two wins at 20f suggest the step to 22f-plus is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Jaramillo
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile that has posted a series of mid-division finishes at 20f in Good ground; the step up to 23f here is potentially interesting but a string of 3-6-5-6-8 results suggests he is finding it hard to land a blow at present, and a 10lb claimer handling the tactics adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Juan Bermudez
runners_data.note: Solid trainer-and-horse combination on fast ground (14/15, 2 wins) and the tongue-tie has been a feature of his better runs; he races as a prominent type by nature, but the density of forward-going horses in this field means he is likely to find himself further back than ideal, which tempers confidence in his raw form figures.

runners_data.name: Time To Bite
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with clear front-running intent confirmed by hood and a career that shows 6 wins from 10 placed efforts in similar ground; his two runs at 26f here are encouraging and 48 days since last run is fine — the risk is purely whether the prominent brigade close him down after the final flight.

runners_data.name: Notnowlinda
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton team up just 16 days after her last start, strongly suggesting she is in good order and fit; a hold-up mare whose four most recent finishes are all 3rd-to-5th, she has not won on Good (0/9) which is a notable concern, and she needs a genuinely run race to deliver her best.

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Veteran of 13 who races as a hold-up type by instinct and carries a visor today; though the map places him in midfield, he is a genuine closer who will likely be hunting late ground — his two most recent placed efforts came on Soft, and this Good surface combined with his age makes him harder to trust even if the race develops in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Time To Bite is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at 11 years old with a clear front-running profile and hood, will set out to control this from the front at a sustainable Good-ground gallop over 2m6f — no rival is likely to seriously challenge for the lead, meaning the pace should be genuine but not searingly hot. Roaring Home, Porter In The Park, and Jackstell are all naturally prominent types who will look to settle just off the leader, creating a compact early order with three horses likely to race in close proximity behind Time To Bite. The hold-up horses — Jaramillo, Notnowlinda, and the redistributed Dinons — will be forced to track further back than ideal, while Juan Bermudez, a true prominent type, has been mapped to midfield because there are more front-running and prominent horses in this field than can all secure their natural position, with Roaring Home and Jackstell best placed to lock up the prominent berths ahead of him. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate, so Juan Bermudez and, to a lesser degree, Porter In The Park may find themselves racing further back than suits. A controlled, even-paced tempo over this trip on Good ground strongly favours prominent racers who can travel into the race and produce a sustained finish — closers face too much ground to make up from too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Time To Bite sets an honest but uncontested pace and the prominent horses travel smoothly into contention from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Time To Bite's unchallenged lead creates a falsely even gallop that suits horses able to race prominently and attack the final two hurdles from a handy position; the 2m6f trip on Good ground rewards those who travel well rather than those who wait. Roaring Home and Jackstell are ideally placed to strike, with their consistent form at this trip and going profile making them the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Time To Bite steals enough of a march early and the pace is so steady that pursuers never quite reel him in.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to press Time To Bite, he could control the fractions entirely, conserving enough energy to hold on through the final flight at 2m6f on forgiving Good ground; his recent course form over this exact trip (2nd, 3rd, 1st) shows he handles this test well. This scenario rewards the front-runner directly and any horse who tracked closest — Porter In The Park's patient prominent style could see her inherit a place.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a race for late finishers and the prominent horses tie up.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop — perhaps sparked by Jackstell or Roaring Home pressing Time To Bite — could open the race up for Jaramillo or Notnowlinda to close from off the pace in the straight; Notnowlinda arrives with a quick turnaround (16 days) and Skelton booking, which hints connections believe she is fit and ready. Jaramillo's hold-up profile suits this shape but his recent string of mid-pack finishes over shorter trips is a concern at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses race too keenly early and the pace collapses in the straight, opening a gap for Juan Bermudez or Dinons.
scenarios.body: Juan Bermudez is a naturally prominent horse forced into midfield by the race shape, meaning he would need others to collapse rather than producing a true style-fit performance; Dinons, a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield, faces a similar misalignment. Both carry style-fit discounts that make this the least likely scenario, reliant on multiple horses racing out of character and underperforming.

watchPoints.text: Time To Bite's ability to control fractions unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaper — watch how quickly he establishes a lead at the start, as any rival that decides to press him changes the entire complexion.

Roaring Home and Jackstell are both natural prominent types who will want to be in the same piece of ground in the early stages — monitor which settles better and which gets shuffled wide or keen, as that will separate their finishing chances.

Notnowlinda's rapid 16-day turnaround with Harry Skelton booked signals trainer confidence, but her zero wins from nine starts on Good ground is a firm flag — watch how she travels into the back straight before committing to her chance.

Juan Bermudez is likely to find himself further back than connections ideally want given the prominent traffic ahead — if Lilly Pinchin is seen pushing along to hold position in the first mile, treat that as a sign the race shape is working against him.

Porter In The Park's 94-day absence and the use of a 7lb claimer for Emma Lavelle, who has had 7 runners in 14 days, is worth tracking in the paddock — if she moves well pre-race, the strong 13/15 similar-going record makes the layoff less of a deterrent.

races.name: Envesca Safety Champions Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a strong recent record, winning twice in his last five and showing solid form on Good ground (9/12 in similar conditions); Jack Andrews rides and the 21-day absence is well within tolerance — the 2m6½f trip suits his staying profile perfectly.

runners_data.name: Premier Fantasy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who handles Good ground well (5/5 in similar), with Nick Scholfield's yard in decent form (2/15 in 14 days); ran just nine days ago which raises fitness questions at 2m6½f, and his recent form string of 1-2-5-3-2 shows consistency without dominating.

runners_data.name: A Dublin Job
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will go for the early lead alongside Gone In Sixty; Cameron Johnstone-Baker (7lb claim) is on board but recent form of 5-6-5-5-6 is uninspiring, and the visor headgear is retained — likely to set the gallop but questionable whether he can sustain it.

runners_data.name: Jack Doyen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent recent form (1-1-2-1-U) with two wins on Good and two overall in his last five; the blinkers are applied and Ben Case's yard is currently flat (0/6 in 14 days) — but his jumping form and trip experience make him one of the most dangerous prominent types in the race.

runners_data.name: Danny's Friend
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 74 days off, but wins on Good ground and the 2m1f+ range suit him; Jack Tudor is a strong booking and Christian Williams' runners often need a run, though his last start was a win — the longer layoff and step up past his typical distances are the key queries.

runners_data.name: On The Platform
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with headgear (p) applied, returning after 62 days; Belinda Clarke's yard has had no runners in the last 14 days, and his Good-ground record is modest (7/15), though he does have a win at 2m4f — moderate form figures of P-1-P-5-5 suggest inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with an outstanding Good-ground record (14/15) and Sean Bowen in the plate, which is a major positive; Alex Hales had one winner from six in the last 14 days — this horse will contest the lead and is the more dangerous of the two pace-setters based on proven jumping ability and consistency.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Posted
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural style is compromised here — the pace map places him in midfield only because true rear-of-field positions are over-subscribed; tagged as fading in the finish and with a form line of P-P-6-5-8 and zero wins, his ability to land a blow is limited even if he finds his position.

runners_data.name: Bahtiyar
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground record (15/15 in similar going) and six places from his last five is a positive angle, but this is a natural hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role by the pace-heavy field shape; Ben Poste takes over from the trainer yard with just one runner in 14 days, and his ceiling at OR 75 may be tested.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form of 3-3-3-0-7 shows consistency at a low level; David Noonan partners for Nigel Hawke's yard (0/2 in 14 days) and the horse handles Good ground reasonably well at around 2m1-3f — unlikely to win but could plug on for a minor share at a long trip.

runners_data.name: Honneur De Sivola
runners_data.note: Has been off 165 days and has pulled up twice in recent starts — a genuine hold-up type who is being mapped forward by the crowded rear of the field; the tongue-tie is in use for Clare Hobson's yard (0/2 in 14 days), and this combination of layoff, declining form, and compromised running style makes a winning performance very unlikely.

races.paceDynamic: A Dublin Job and Gone In Sixty are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 2m6½f trip at Stratford, creating an honest, competitive gallop that is unlikely to collapse into a crawl at any stage. With two genuine pace horses pressing each other, the tempo should be sustained throughout, gradually stretching the field and placing a premium on stamina and jumping fluency over the final circuit. Jack Doyen and On The Platform will look to sit prominently just behind the front two and are best placed to pounce if either leader falters, while the true hold-up brigade — Keep Me Posted, Bahtiyar, and Honneur De Sivola — are mapped to midfield only because the rear is over-subscribed, meaning their true late-running profiles are compromised by this contest's shape. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-patient closers who travel comfortably in the slipstream of contested pace and stay on powerfully from three out, rather than pure hold-up horses who need the field to come back to them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If A Dublin Job and Gone In Sixty press each other into a genuine gallop and the front two tire from three out, allowing prominent-to-midfield chasers to pick them off.
scenarios.body: The sustained dual pace sets up a searching test that exposes the front-runners in the closing stages, with horses like Huckleberry Sting and Danny's Friend, who travel within themselves and finish strongly on Good ground, ideally positioned to swoop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Doyen or On The Platform settle just off the pace and the front two soften each other enough for a well-placed chaser to coast into the lead at the third-last.
scenarios.body: A prominent racer who handles the Good surface and has the jumping accuracy to maintain rhythm at this distance will inherit the lead without having to accelerate sharply, making it a test of class and soundness from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters (most likely Gone In Sixty, who has class and a strong Good-ground record) edges away from its rival early and is permitted an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine head-to-head battle for the lead, the gallop settles to a rhythm that suits the bold-jumping front-runner, and with the hold-up horses trapped in traffic or racing out of role, no sustained late challenge materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the redistributed hold-up horses (Keep Me Posted, Bahtiyar, Honneur De Sivola) somehow secure their natural rearward position and produce a powerful late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario is markedly discounted because all three genuine hold-up types are racing out of role in this pace-heavy shape, reducing their ability to deliver the sweeping late finish their profiles require.

watchPoints.text: Gone In Sixty and A Dublin Job will fight for the early lead — watch whether one gains a clear advantage by the first fence, as a front-runner allowed to dominate unchallenged transforms the race shape entirely.

Jack Doyen has unseated recently (U in last run) — monitor his jumping at the early fences, as a bold-jumping error at Stratford's tight turns could eliminate the most dangerous prominent racer in the field.

Keep Me Posted, Bahtiyar, and Honneur De Sivola are genuine hold-up horses operating out of position — if midfield becomes congested on the first circuit, traffic trouble could affect all three simultaneously without any of them delivering a meaningful challenge.

Danny's Friend returns after 74 days for Christian Williams — yards that don't need a pipe-opener often target a win first time back, and Jack Tudor's presence suggests intent, but the step up in trip and distance beyond his winning range bears watching.

Honneur De Sivola's 165-day absence combined with two recent pull-ups makes him a significant jumping risk — a loose horse in a field of 11 over 2m6½f could disrupt the pace dynamic if he exits the race early.

races.name: Andy Townsend Memorial Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Mistral Blue
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner rated 99 who gets to lead entirely unchallenged here; Good ground suits (12/15 sim-going), Fergal O'Brien in decent 14-day form, and at 8 years old she is battle-hardened — Fern O'Brien's 5lb claim helps offset the top weight of 168lbs.

runners_data.name: Leave Her To Me
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer on 51 days off last run, best form came on Good going over shorter trips; at OR 98 she has the class but will need the pace to be stronger than anticipated to reel in the front-runners from off the bridle.

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare with six recent placed efforts on Good ground (11/15 sim-going), including two seconds; tongue tie noted, Miss Imogen Mathias claims 7lbs, and her reliable jumping and stamina profile over 22-24f give her the best credentials of the hold-up brigade.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Tongue tie applied for this 6-year-old, who has placed four times in recent starts without winning; Good ground is fine but a string of fourths suggests she finds a way to finish just behind the money — J M Quinlan takes the ride in what is a moderate pace shape for a hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Lady Bee Great
runners_data.note: Recent form reads 118 and her last two wins were on Good, but she carries a finishing fade flag and is a genuine hold-up horse pushed forward on the map only by the density of rear-runners in this field — Stan Sheppard rides, and she will need to be ridden closer to the pace than is natural.

runners_data.name: Liasse d'Argent
runners_data.note: Returning from 98 days off for Tom Gretton, who has no 14-day runners to reference; a true hold-up type squeezed toward midfield on the map, she is 0W0P on Good in the sim-going sample and needs significant improvement on recent form figures of 56-46 to feature.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: The one horse who can genuinely track Mistral Blue in the early stages, having shown prominent-race tendencies in his profile (2W7P sim-going); at OR 80 he is lower-rated than the market leaders but his tactical position just behind the leader could make him dangerous if the pace is fair.

runners_data.name: Sadies Diamond
runners_data.note: Just 7 days since her last run for Jeff Mullins (1/9 in 14 days), and while she has placed on Good going before, she is a natural hold-up horse who will struggle to get competitive from her true position in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring her into contention.

runners_data.name: Porridge
runners_data.note: Returning after 88 days for Tracey Leeson with no 14-day runners; form reads P4-88P and she has failed to complete or struggled on Good-ish ground before — a genuine hold-up type on the map only by redistribution, with form that offers little encouragement even in a more favourable shape.

runners_data.name: Mc'flo
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at 5 with the lowest OR (70), returning 11 days after her last run for Anthony Carso (0/3 in 14 days); a natural hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map, her recent string of 8964P5 form figures make her a long-shot even if the pace shape were ideal for closers.

races.paceDynamic: Mistral Blue is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner mares' handicap hurdle over 2m6f at Stratford on Good ground, and with no genuine rival likely to push her from the front, she is set to control proceedings at a sustainable, measured gallop throughout. Quick Of The Night is the only other horse with any prominent claims and may track Mistral Blue through the early and middle stages, but neither horse is likely to inject the kind of pressure that would make this a truly searching test. With the pace uncontested and the tempo likely to be modest, this race shape heavily favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken from the front or just off it, rather than true hold-up types who need a strong gallop to get into contention from off the pace. The field holds considerably more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Lady Bee Great, Liasse d'Argent, Sadies Diamond, Porridge and Mc'flo are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, with none realistically able to secure their preferred late-running position in a race where pace is likely to be slow and the winning move will come from the front; Mistral Blue and Quick Of The Night are best placed to dictate, and the pace shape squarely favours prominent racers who can dominate from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mistral Blue Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Mistral Blue leads from the front without pressure and sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Mistral Blue dictates every yard at a fair but unhurried tempo, leaving hold-up horses with no pace to aim at and creating an unwinnable task for those who need to close from deep; horses who can travel close to the leader and produce a clean jump at the last hurdle are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Of The Night tracks Mistral Blue aggressively and the two set a genuinely strong pace that grinds out hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A contested front sets a stronger early tempo that drains stamina reserves from further back, turning the race into a test of staying power rather than a finishing sprint; horses with proven stamina at the trip who can race prominently are rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and creates enough of a true gallop that a hold-up horse can run down the leaders.
scenarios.body: With a genuine gallop in place, horses coming from midfield find the rail and the final flight to pick off tired front-runners; Parikarma and Leave Her To Me, who are proven on Good and at comparable trips, are best equipped to benefit if a gap opens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches, a faller or interference disrupts the pace, or a complete messy crawl turns the finish into a sprint lottery.
scenarios.body: With a field full of horses out of their preferred running position, any disruption to the expected order causes a scramble in the straight that could flatter shorter-priced horses or produce a big-price outcome; Lady Bee Great's recent form of 118 gives her more tactical versatility than most of the redistributed hold-up types.

watchPoints.text: Mistral Blue sets the pace unchallenged — if she jumps cleanly and is allowed to bowl along at her own rhythm, the race could be over as a contest turning for home; watch for any jump errors that allow Quick Of The Night to close or take over.

Parikarma is the best-credentialled hold-up horse in the field and has been placed six times on Good; watch whether Miss Imogen Mathias elects to push her closer than usual given the lack of true pace, which could transform her finishing chance.

Lady Bee Great's finishing-fade flag is a significant concern over 2m6f in a slow-run race — if Stan Sheppard sends her forward to compensate, she may not last home, and if he doesn't, she may never get competitive.

Five hold-up horses (Lady Bee Great, Liasse d'Argent, Sadies Diamond, Porridge, Mc'flo) are all naturally drawn toward the rear but cannot all get there in a 10-runner field — watch the first half-mile for potential jostling and unexpected positional changes that could affect who travels best.

Liasse d'Argent and Porridge are both returning from lengthy breaks (98 and 88 days respectively) with trainers showing no recent runners — treat first-time-back fitness as a genuine unknown and watch how both travel early before projecting any late improvement.
